turns.text: Why does YOLO deserve its own place in the history of artificial intelligence?
Before YOLO, high-accuracy detectors often relied on multi-stage pipelines. YOLO asked what would happen if detection became one dense prediction problem.

The image is divided into a grid; each cell predicts boxes, confidence, and classes, all in one forward pass. The key mechanism is Single-shot grid-based object detection, which links the source material to the visible demo behavior.

Experts generally treat YOLO as the system that made real-time object detection a central benchmark goal. Its long-term legacy is the framing of detection as fast single-pass prediction, influencing many later detector families and deployment expectations.
As today's systems grow larger, which lessons from YOLO still matter, and which limits deserve to be questioned again?
